narrative:
The model estimated a 43% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. That is not a certainty, but it was high enough under the lender’s decision threshold for your application to be denied.

The most influential factor in the decision was the short length of the requested credit: 10 months versus an approved-applicant average of about 19 months. This worked in your favour and pushed the assessment toward good credit. The second most important factor was your checking-account status of 0–200 DM, and this was the main adverse factor, pushing toward bad credit. Among approved applicants, having no checking account was much more common than a 0–200 DM balance, so this profile stood out as a risk signal. The third most important factor was the requested amount: 1,521 DM, well below the approved average of about 3,020 DM. That also helped your case by pushing toward good credit.

Overall, your shorter credit period and lower amount helped, but they were not enough to offset the concern raised by your checking-account position and the rest of your profile. To improve your chances next time, focus on strengthening your checking-account status—for example, maintaining a higher balance and avoiding overdrafts—and ask the lender what account history or balance would meet its criteria before reapplying.
